primary_evidence: Strong replays use peak hands 8/10/12/12/12/12; Q2 elite replays use 12 hands and high productive surface, but X1.14 aggressive workforce regressed required seeds.
Peak hands vary: Sokolov 8, Hutchinson 10, truebelief 12, Q2 top replays 12. No single hand count explains score.
High scores correlate with sustained hiring and throughput; last/first hire timing needs finer ledger extraction before a causal claim.
Q2 replays convert 3103-3229 productive actions into 96k-133k; Sokolov has fewer productive actions but dense monetization. Productive action count alone is insufficient.
Elite Q1/Q2 competitors show low weed tile-days: 10, 11, 5, 26, 24. Sokolov is a counterexample at 145 but still lower/more monetized than our comparable failure.
Q2 elite replays peak at 75 productive tiles and Q1 elites at 46-50, but Sokolov wins with only 15 peak productive tiles.
Sokolov proves compact density can beat our Q1 run; Q2 winners expand early and still monetize. Density matters, but not necessarily before expansion in all seeds.
Poor or premature expansion loses: our 101294736 side bought Q2 Day 8 with low cash/productive base and scored 6825. But disciplined Q2 wins exist.
Q1 is used by truebelief and Hutchinson, absent in Sokolov, and used before Q2 in the high-scoring 3Q replays. Requiredness is false; conditional value is supported.
Old 3-replay batch had no competitor Q2, but new Q2 files include 96k-133k scores with Q2 Day 9-11 and 75 peak productive tiles.
All strong competitors include livestock products: Milk, Fertilizer, Wool and sometimes Egg. Final livestock ranges from 4 Cow/2 Sheep to 13 Cow/2 Sheep and 6 Cow/9 Sheep.
Observed livestock mixes differ: 9C/5S, 7C/4S/2G, 4C/2S, 6C/9S, 13C/2S, 12C.
Every competitor sells multiple channels: Wheat, Milk, Fertilizer, premium crops, Wool, and sometimes Egg/Tomato.
Cash is visible, but committed working capital, expected payback and activation cost are not directly present in replay state summaries.
Endgame liquidation/no-planting can be inferred from late sells and final cash, but requires per-day action ledger to classify precisely.

claim: HIRE based on marginal monetizable throughput
primary_evidence: The desired decision rule is not directly observable from replay actions; only realized hires and output are visible.
Low weeds accompany elite scores in most replays, but X1.14 reduced weeds while lowering money and Sokolov tolerated 145 weed tile-days.
Sokolov beats our higher-surface run with lower peak productive tiles; Q2 top runs show high physical utilization plus high monetization.
High sell counts and broad products imply collection/sell throughput, but exact uncollected yield and route efficiency need a ledger.
Competitors buy and sell Wheat; our comparable sides sell extreme Wheat volumes. Without price/inventory ledger, profit/waste cannot be concluded.
Diversified buys are visible across competitors, but exact Day-1 constants differ and are reference trajectories only.
Two 86k/90k Q1-only elites support sufficiency, Sokolov Q0-only beats us, but Q2 elites reach 96k-133k.
Crop/product mixes vary and late liquidation is plausible, but horizon-aware intent is not directly observable.
Low weeds correlate with elite Q1/Q2 results, but X1.14 clean-field variants regressed and Sokolov wins despite high weeds.
